policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Now there was a certain man in Caesarea' supplies the copula that English requires of a verbless Greek clause, so 'there was' does not show whether the exemplar printed a separate ἦν.
ASV 'who gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God always' carries no connective at the participle; the added τε is a link English leaves unrendered either way.
ASV renders two approximating words, 'as it were about the ninth hour', i.e. ὡσεὶ plus περὶ; the omission would leave only ὡσεὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην, for which 'as it were about' is doubled.
ASV 'before God' renders ἔμπροσθεν and ἐνώπιον alike; the two prepositions are indistinguishable in English.
Word order only: ASV 'send men to Joppa' follows English order and cannot show whether ἄνδρας stood before or after εἰς Ἰόππην.

ASV 'fetch one Simon, who is surnamed Peter' renders the indefinite τινα ('one Simon') and a finite relative clause 'who is surnamed'; RP's τὸν ἐπικαλούμενον Πέτρον has no indefinite and an attributive participle.
ASV 'the angel that spake unto him' has the pronoun, not the proper name that RP's τῷ Κορνηλίῳ would give ('spake unto Cornelius').
ASV 'two of his household-servants' could render either the added αὐτοῦ or the bare article τῶν οἰκετῶν, which English idiomatically turns into a possessive; the possessive does not settle the unit.
Word order only: 'having rehearsed all things unto them' fixes the English order regardless of whether ἅπαντα preceded or followed αὐτοῖς.
ASV 'while they made ready' renders the genitive-absolute subject as a plain pronoun, which serves αὐτῶν and ἐκείνων equally.
ASV recasts with the man as subject, 'he fell into a trance'; that idiom answers both 'a trance came upon him' (ἐγένετο) and 'fell upon him' (ἐπέπεσεν).
ASV has 'a certain vessel descending' with no 'upon him'; RP's added ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν would be rendered, as the parallel ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς is rendered 'upon the earth'.
ASV reads 'let down by four corners upon the earth' with no 'bound'; RP's added δεδεμένον καὶ would give 'bound at the four corners and let down'.
ASV lists only 'fourfooted beasts and creeping things of the earth and birds of the heaven'; RP's τὰ θηρία (wild beasts) is a fourth member that ASV does not render.
ASV 'anything that is common and unclean' renders the conjunction καὶ, not the disjunctive ἢ ('or unclean').
ASV 'and straightway the vessel was received up' renders εὐθὺς; RP's πάλιν would give 'again was received up'.
ASV 'behold, the men that were sent' begins the apodosis after a genitive absolute, where a resumptive καί is regularly left untranslated; its absence in English does not exclude καὶ ἰδού.
ASV 'sent by Cornelius' renders the agent phrase alike for ὑπὸ and ἀπὸ.
The article on the proper name Σίμωνος has no English exponent: 'Simon's house' is the rendering with or without τοῦ.
ASV 'called and asked' uses a simple past that renders the imperfect ἐπυνθάνοντο and the aorist ἐπύθοντο alike.
ASV 'the Spirit said unto him' has the dative pronoun, which excludes WH's r02 (τὸ πνεῦμα alone); the order of αὐτῷ and τὸ πνεῦμα is not recoverable from English.
ASV 'behold, three men seek thee' renders the numeral τρεῖς, excluding both the bare ἄνδρες and WH's δύο ('two').
ASV 'three men seek thee' uses a finite English verb for either the participle ζητοῦντές or the finite ζητοῦσίν.
ASV 'for I have sent them' renders ὅτι and the strengthened διότι identically.
ASV 'he arose and went forth with them' renders the participle ἀναστὰς and keeps the subject pronominal; RP's ὁ Πέτρος would give a named subject and no 'arose'.
ASV opens 'And on the morrow', and ASV renders δέ as 'And' as freely as καί; the connective does not distinguish τῇ δὲ from Καὶ τῇ.
ASV text reads the plural 'they entered into Caesarea' (εἰσῆλθον), and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read he' records the singular εἰσῆλθεν as the rejected alternative.
Word order only: 'Peter raised him up' is the English order for either ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν or αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν.
ASV 'I was keeping the ninth hour of prayer in my house' has no 'fasting'; RP's νηστεύων καὶ would be rendered as it is elsewhere in ASV.
ASV's paraphrase 'the ninth hour of prayer' needs the noun 'hour' with the ordinal in English whether or not ὥραν stood in the Greek.
ASV ends the verse at 'by the sea side'; RP's added ὃς παραγενόμενος λαλήσει σοι ('who when he cometh shall speak unto thee') is absent from the ASV text.
ASV 'commanded thee of the Lord' renders κυρίου; RP's θεοῦ would give 'of God', which ASV uses earlier in the verse for the distinct τοῦ θεοῦ.

ASV text 'The word which he sent unto the children of Israel' renders the relative ὃν, and the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read He sent the word unto' records the omission as the rejected alternative.
ASV 'beginning from Galilee' does not mark the case of the participle, so nominative ἀρξάμενος and accusative ἀρξάμενον are alike in English.
ASV 'And we are witnesses' supplies the copula English requires of a nominal clause, so 'are' does not show whether ἐσμεν stood in the Greek.
ASV 'both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem' repeats the preposition as English coordination invites, which does not establish a second ἐν in the Greek.
ASV 'raised up the third day' renders the dative of time the same with or without ἐν.
ASV 'to testify that this is he who is ordained of God' renders the demonstrative οὗτός ('this'); RP's αὐτός would give 'he is he that is ordained'.
ASV 'as many as came with Peter' renders the correlative ὅσοι; WH's simple relative οἳ would give 'who came with Peter'.
Word order and article only: 'the gift of the Holy Spirit' is the rendering of ἁγίου πνεύματος and πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου alike.
The article before Πέτρος has no English exponent: 'Then answered Peter' stands with or without ὁ.
Word order only: 'Can any man forbid' fixes the English order for either δύναται κωλῦσαί or κωλῦσαί δύναται.
ASV 'as well as we' renders the comparative particle alike for ὡς and καθὼς.
ASV opens 'And he commanded them'; that connective renders δὲ and τε alike.
ASV 'to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ' names Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ; RP's τοῦ κυρίου would give 'in the name of the Lord'.
